facts.text: Stevenson was founded by the Stevenson family from Missouri who claimed land in the Gorge in the 1800s.
In 1893 an unauthorized crew moved Skamania County records from Cascades to Stevenson overnight, making it the county seat.
The Bridge of the Gods, carrying the Pacific Crest Trail, connects Stevenson to Cascade Locks and is the only river crossing between Portland and Hood River.
Stevenson sits on the north bank of the Columbia River within the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area, about 45 miles east of Portland.
The Columbia Gorge Museum in Stevenson interprets the natural and cultural heritage of the Gorge, while Skamania Lodge offers luxury lodging.
The city’s waterfront at Bob’s Beach is a launch spot for windsurfers and kiteboarders thanks to dependable winds in the widened river.
